articles.title: Stephen Hawking seen lounging between 2 bikini-clad women as scientist’s ties to Epstein return to spotlight
articles.summary: A viral photo showing the late scientist Stephen Hawking with bikini-clad women has reignited discussions about his alleged connections to Jeffrey Epstein. This development brings renewed scrutiny to Hawking's associations and the broader implications of Epstein's controversial network. For aspirants, it underscores how high-profile figures, even posthumously, face intense media scrutiny regarding their past links.

articles.title: VyOS: VyOS Stream 2026.02 is available for download
articles.summary: VyOS has released Stream 2026.02, an update for its network operating system, now available for download. This version includes significant backports from the rolling release, enhancing its capabilities. Key new features highlighted are TLS support for syslog, improving secure logging; NAT66 source groups for advanced network address translation; and IPFIX support, which aids in flexible flow data export and network monitoring.

articles.title: Is the USPTO Flagging Selected Patent Applications for Extra Scrutiny—Again?
articles.summary: A federal court battle challenges the USPTO's authority to indefinitely shelve patent applications flagged as 'of special interest.' The core dispute centers on whether the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office truly lacks discretion to halt processing applications without clear legal grounds. This case holds significant implications for patent law and the timely progression of technological innovations.

articles.title: India becoming global manufacturing hub for smartphones as exports hit $30 billion: Ashwini Vaishnaw
articles.summary: India is rapidly emerging as the world's smartphone manufacturing hub, with Union Electronics and IT Minister Ashwin stating that exports are projected to hit an ambitious $30 billion for the calendar year 2025. This significant growth underscores India's rising capabilities in high-tech manufacturing and its increasing economic footprint globally, boosting national development and industrial self-reliance.

articles.title: Diesel Engines Need Oxygen, So How Do Submarines Use Them Underwater?
articles.summary: A diesel engine functions by compressing air within its cylinders, significantly raising its temperature. Fuel is then injected into this hot air, leading to ignition and a forceful combustion. This resulting force drives pistons, which converts the energy into mechanical power to propel the vehicle's main gears. This fundamental process is key to the engine's operation and performance.

articles.title: Defence indigenization: How securing India’s strategic autonomy has taken centre-stage
articles.summary: India's defence budget has witnessed a significant increase over the past decade, rising from 2.53 trillion in 2013-14 by 5.32 trillion. This substantial financial growth underscores the nation's strategic focus on bolstering its defence capabilities and modernizing its armed forces. The rise reflects a concerted effort to enhance national security and achieve greater self-reliance in military preparedness, crucial for regional stability.
